q: Which club finished third in the 2007-08 Eredivisie, behind PSV and Ajax?
sub: A club record 63 points under Ernie Brandts, told in January his contract would not be renewed.
note: Table and 63 points confirmed on nl.wikipedia Eredivisie 2007/08. Brandts and the January 2008 contract news confirmed on his nl page. Cut the phrase highest finish in its history: it holds only for the Eredivisie era, NAC were national champions in 1921.

q: Which Limburg club lost the 2008 KNVB Cup final 2-0 to Feyenoord, with goals from Denny Landzaat and Jonathan de Guzman?
sub: Played at De Kuip on 27 April 2008 in front of 51,177, Feyenoord's eleventh cup.
note: Final, scorers and minutes confirmed on nl.wikipedia KNVB beker 2007/08. Attendance was 51,177, not 46,000.

q: Which club won the 2007-08 Eerste Divisie under Stanley Menzo, then finished bottom of the Eredivisie the very next season?
sub: Frans Adelaar was the coach for the relegation season, Menzo having left.
note: FC Volendam won the 2007-08 Eerste Divisie under Stanley Menzo on 77 points and finished 18th in 2008-09 under Frans Adelaar. Both confirmed.

q: Roda JC finished 16th in 2008-09 and had to play the play-offs. Which Frisian club did they beat to stay up?
sub: It went to a third match and a penalty shoot-out before Roda survived.
note: Roda 16th and the Cambuur tie confirmed on nl.wikipedia Play-offs 2009: 0-0, 1-1, then 2-2 in the decider, Roda winning 5-3 on penalties. The old sub said extra time decided it.

q: VVV won the 2008-09 Eerste Divisie with Keisuke Honda as the star, but who was their top scorer, with 25 goals?
sub: Honda took the first Gouden Stier as the division's best player.
note: Calabro 25 goals and the Gouden Stier confirmed. Honda's total is disputed, 16 on both his Wikipedia pages but 14 on the Eerste divisie 2008/09 page, so the number is out of the sub.

q: From which Japanese club did VVV-Venlo sign Keisuke Honda in January 2008?
sub: His first six months in Venlo ended in relegation, the first of his career.
note: Nagoya Grampus, January 2008, confirmed on the English Honda article, and VVV were relegated that season.

q: Which Russian club did Keisuke Honda leave VVV-Venlo for at the end of 2009?
sub: Yoshida followed him from Nagoya Grampus to Venlo that same month.
note: CSKA agreement of 31 December 2009 confirmed. Yoshida joined VVV in December 2009, not later, and the agent detail is about Honda introducing his agent to Yoshida, not to VVV. Retiered: a serious fan knows this move.

q: Mounir El Hamdaoui was Eredivisie top scorer with AZ in 2008-09. Which club had he joined AZ from in 2007?
sub: He was also named Dutch Footballer of the Year that season.
note: El Hamdaoui joined AZ from Willem II in 2007, 23 goals as top scorer and Dutch Footballer of the Year in 2008-09. Confirmed.

q: Which Costa Rican scored 24 league goals for Twente in 2009-10 and opened the scoring at NAC on the day the title was won?
sub: Twente won 2-0 in Breda on 2 May 2010, Stoch adding the second.
note: 24 league goals, the 23rd minute opener at NAC on 2 May 2010 and Stoch's second are all confirmed. Retiered: Twente's title day is serious-fan, not anorak.

q: Which Twente player scored in the 118th minute of the 2009 KNVB Cup final and then missed in the shoot-out?
sub: Gerald Sibon converted the winning penalty for Heerenveen, 5-4.
note: Hersi scored in the 118th minute and missed his penalty, Sibon converted for 5-4. Confirmed on the 2009 final article.

q: Which Serbian winger did Ajax sign from Heerenveen in 2008 for 16.25 million euros, then a Dutch transfer record?
sub: He had scored 15 league goals in one season in Friesland.
note: 16.25 million euros and the Dutch record confirmed on nl.wikipedia. He scored 15 league goals in 2007-08, not 14.

q: Heracles finished sixth in 2009-10, then their best ever. Who was the coach, who left for AZ that summer?
sub: He opened that season by beating champions AZ 3-2.
note: Sixth place, best ever at the time, Verbeek leaving for AZ and the 3-2 win over champions AZ on the opening day are all confirmed.

q: RKC Waalwijk went down in 2009-10 with 15 points from five wins. How many draws did they manage all season?
sub: They conceded 80 goals and went straight back to the Eerste Divisie.
note: 15 points, five wins, no draws, 29 defeats and 80 conceded. Confirmed on the nl season article.

q: Who did AZ appoint to follow Louis van Gaal in 2009, and sack on 5 December that year after seven league defeats in sixteen games?
sub: Dick Advocaat took over the reigning champions.
note: Koeman followed Van Gaal, was sacked on 5 December 2009 after a seventh league defeat in sixteen games, Advocaat came in on 10 December. Confirmed.

q: Excelsior stayed up in 2011 by winning a play-off final 5-1 away and 4-2 at home. Who were the opponents?
sub: Nine goals over two legs against a club that had not been in the top flight since 1984.
note: 5-1 away at Helmond Sport then 4-2 at home confirmed on nl.wikipedia Play-offs 2011. Helmond last played in the Eredivisie in 1983-84.

q: Which Russian striker, on loan from Anderlecht, scored 21 league goals for ADO Den Haag in 2010-11?
sub: He joined Ajax on a free that summer and won the title.
note: 21 league goals on loan from Anderlecht, then Ajax on a free in 2011 and the title. Confirmed.

q: Which Dane scored NEC's winner away at Spartak Moscow in December 2008 and left for Ajax on a free in 2012?
sub: He had come to Nijmegen from De Graafschap in 2008.
note: Spartak winner in December 2008, arrival from De Graafschap in 2008 and the free move to Ajax in 2012 confirmed.

q: NEC came through a 2008-09 UEFA Cup group with Tottenham, Udinese, Spartak and Dinamo Zagreb. Who beat them 3-0 in Nijmegen in the next round?
sub: Hamburg won the return 1-0 as well.
note: Group D with Tottenham, Udinese, Spartak and Dinamo Zagreb, then 0-3 in Nijmegen and 1-0 in Hamburg. Confirmed.

q: Which Frisian club won the 2012-13 Eerste Divisie, returning to the Eredivisie after thirteen years away?
sub: Cambuur had not been in the top flight since 1999-2000.
note: Cambuur and the thirteen years confirmed, but Dwight Lodeweges was not the coach: Alfons Arts started the season and was sacked on 22 March 2013, Henk de Jong and Jan Bruin finished it. Lodeweges only arrived for 2013-14.

q: FC Zwolle clinched the 2011-12 Eerste Divisie title on Friday 13 April 2012 with a 0-0 draw against which club?
sub: The next day the club announced it would go back to the name PEC Zwolle.
note: 0-0 against FC Eindhoven on Friday 13 April 2012 and the PEC name announcement the next day, confirmed on nl.wikipedia PEC Zwolle.

q: Which Ivorian scored 31 goals in 30 league games for Vitesse in 2012-13 and joined Swansea for a club record 12 million pounds?
sub: He was also named Dutch Footballer of the Year.
note: 31 goals in 30 games, 12 million pounds to Swansea and the Dutch Footballer of the Year award confirmed. Retiered: Bony at Vitesse is common knowledge for a regular watcher.

q: Which American scored AZ's second goal in the 2013 KNVB Cup final against PSV, two minutes after Adam Maher had opened the scoring?
sub: AZ won 2-1, their first cup since 1982.
note: Maher in the 12th minute, Altidore in the 14th, 2-1, and AZ had last won the cup in 1982. Confirmed.

q: Go Ahead Eagles won the 2013 play-off final 3-0 at home and lost the return 1-0. Who were the opponents?
sub: Erik ten Hag's Eagles ended seventeen years outside the top flight.
note: 3-0 at home then 1-0 away to Volendam, Erik ten Hag, seventeen years out. Confirmed on the nl season article.

q: Roda JC stayed up in 2013 by winning the play-off second leg 6-1 at home. Which club did they beat?
sub: The first leg in Doetinchem had been 1-1.
note: Legs were the wrong way round. Play-offs 2013: 1-1 at De Vijverberg, then 6-1 for Roda in Kerkrade, so the 6-1 was at home, not away.

q: Which Rotterdam club relegated NEC in the 2014 play-offs, winning 1-0 at home and 3-1 in Nijmegen?
sub: It ended twenty straight NEC seasons in the Eredivisie.
note: Sparta won 1-0 at Het Kasteel and 3-1 in Nijmegen, ending a twenty-year NEC run. Confirmed.

q: Who scored twice in the first half of the 2014 KNVB Cup final for PEC Zwolle against Ajax, a nineteen-year-old New Zealander?
sub: Guyon Fernandez also scored twice and Bram van Polen made it 5-1.
note: Ryan Thomas scored in the 8th and 12th minutes, Fernandez twice, Van Polen for 5-1, and he was 19. Confirmed.

q: Which Icelander was Eredivisie top scorer in 2013-14 with 29 goals for Heerenveen?
sub: Real Sociedad paid 7.5 million euros for him that summer.
note: 29 goals, Iceland, 7.5 million euros to Real Sociedad, all confirmed. Retiered: a regular watcher remembers Finnbogason.

q: Which Slovak scored both goals when Groningen beat PEC Zwolle 2-0 in the 2015 KNVB Cup final?
sub: Jarchinio Antonia set up the second one.
note: Rusnak scored both, in the 64th and 75th minutes. Only the second was assisted by Antonia, so the sub overreached.

q: NEC won the 2014-15 Eerste Divisie with 101 points and 100 goals. Who was the coach?
sub: Sjoerd Ars scored 28 of the goals.
note: 101 points, 100 goals, Ruud Brood and the 28 goals confirmed, but NEC did not win all four period titles: they took periods one and four, Almere City took two and FC Oss three.

q: Roda JC went straight back up in 2015 with a 110th-minute winner at NAC in the play-off final. Who scored it?
sub: Roda lost the first leg 1-0 at home and won 2-1 in Breda after extra time.
note: Van Hyfte scored in the 110th minute in Breda after Roda lost the first leg 1-0 at home. Confirmed on Play-offs 2015.

q: Which Rotterdam club won the 2015-16 Eerste Divisie under Alex Pastoor, sealing it with a 3-1 win over Jong Ajax?
sub: Six years after going down on away goals to Excelsior.
note: Sparta took the 2015-16 title under Pastoor with a 3-1 win over Jong Ajax, six years after the 2010 away-goals relegation. Confirmed.

q: Heracles played their first ever European tie in 2016 and went out on away goals after 1-1 and 0-0. Who were the opponents?
sub: Third qualifying round of the Europa League.
note: 1-1 at home then 0-0 in Portugal against Arouca, out on away goals in the third qualifying round. Confirmed.

q: Which Turkish businessman, a former Galatasaray executive, took control of Fortuna Sittard in 2016?
sub: Fortuna had been in the Eerste Divisie since 2002.
note: Isitan Gun, Turkish, former Galatasaray chief operating officer, confirmed. The fourteenth straight season count did not check out: Fortuna went down in 2002, so 2016-17 was their fifteenth.

q: Which Nigerian, a former Ajax midfielder, coached Fortuna Sittard from December 2016 until his suspension in February 2018?
sub: Fortuna went up three months after he was removed.
note: Appointed 27 December 2016, suspended 14 February 2018, Nigerian, an Ajax midfielder from 1997 to 1999. Confirmed.

q: Fortuna Sittard sealed promotion in 2018 with a 1-0 win over which reserve side?
sub: Fortuna finished second, one point behind Jong Ajax, who could not go up.
note: 1-0 against Jong PSV, second on 78 points, one behind champions Jong Ajax who could not be promoted. Confirmed on the Eerste divisie 2017/18 table.

q: Which Portuguese interim coach, with Kevin Hofland as assistant, took Fortuna Sittard over the line to promotion in 2018?
sub: He took over after Sunday Oliseh was suspended on 14 February.
note: Claudio Braga, Portuguese, took over with Kevin Hofland after Oliseh was removed on 14 February 2018 and went unbeaten to the end. Confirmed.

q: Which Belgian striker scored a hat-trick as NAC won 4-1 at NEC in the 2017 play-off final to go up?
sub: He also scored the only goal of the first leg in Breda.
note: Dessers scored three in the 4-1 at NEC on 28 May 2017 and the only goal of the first leg in Breda. Confirmed on Play-offs 2017.

q: Which Chelsea loanee was Vitesse's player of the year in 2017-18 and scored in the European play-off final against Utrecht?
sub: He got a booking in that game that ruled him out of the second leg.
note: Vitesse Player of the Year, scored in the first leg of the European play-off final against Utrecht and was booked, which ruled him out of the second leg. Confirmed.

q: Which AZ winger was the 2017-18 Eredivisie top scorer with 21 goals, the first Asian to top the charts in a major European league?
sub: Brighton paid a club record fee for him that summer.
note: 21 goals, first Asian top scorer in a major European league, club record fee to Brighton, all confirmed. Retiered: a regular watcher knows this one.

q: Which club reached the Eredivisie for the first time ever by winning 3-1 at Sparta's Het Kasteel in May 2018?
sub: The first Drenthe club in the top flight. Sparta went down.
note: 0-0 at Emmen then Emmen won 3-1 at Het Kasteel, a first promotion in their history, Sparta down. Confirmed on Play-offs 2018.

q: Sparta sacked Alex Pastoor on 17 December 2017 after a 7-0 home defeat by Feyenoord. Which veteran coach took over?
sub: Advocaat could not save them, Sparta went down in the play-offs.
note: The 7-0 was at home at Het Kasteel, not away at Feyenoord. Date and Advocaat confirmed by NOS. Sub reworded so it no longer gives away the FC Emmen answer in another row.

q: Roda JC went down in 2018 after 0-0 away and 1-2 at home in the play-offs. Who beat them?
sub: Almere then lost the final to De Graafschap.
note: 0-0 at Almere then 1-2 at home in Kerkrade, and Almere lost the final to De Graafschap. Confirmed.

q: VVV-Venlo clinched promotion on 14 April 2017 with a 2-1 win away at which club?
sub: Maurice Steijn's side took the title a week later.
note: The RKC win sealed promotion, not the title: nl.wikipedia says the championship was settled a week later with a 0-0 at FC Eindhoven. The 80 point total could not be confirmed, so it is out.

q: Who coached VVV-Venlo from 2014 to 2019, winning the 2017 Eerste Divisie title, and later had eleven games in charge of Ajax?
sub: He won the Rinus Michels Award for that title season.
note: VVV from 1 July 2014 to 8 June 2019, the 2017 title, the Rinus Michels Award and eleven games at Ajax, all confirmed.

q: Willem II stayed up in 2016 by winning a play-off final 4-3 on aggregate, Erik Falkenburg scoring twice in the return. Who did they beat?
sub: NAC won the first leg 2-1, Willem II the second 3-1.
note: NAC won the first leg 2-1 in Breda, Willem II won 3-1 with two Falkenburg goals, 4-3 on aggregate. Confirmed.

q: Utrecht beat Celtic 4-0 in August 2010 to reach the Europa League group stage. Who scored a hat-trick?
sub: Celtic had won the first leg 2-0.
note: Hat-trick on 26 August 2010 in a 4-0 win and Celtic's 2-0 first leg confirmed. Retiered: that night is serious-fan territory rather than anorak.

q: Which English club knocked Twente out of the 2008-09 Champions League third qualifying round, winning 2-0 in Enschede and 4-0 at home?
sub: Twente dropped into the UEFA Cup and beat Rennes on away goals.
note: 0-2 in Enschede and 0-4 at the Emirates, then Twente went through against Rennes on away goals after 1-0 and 1-2. Confirmed.

q: Which Spanish club beat NAC Breda 3-1 and then 6-1 in the 2009-10 Europa League play-off round?
sub: NAC had earned Europe by beating Groningen in the 2009 play-offs.
note: 3-1 and 6-1 to Villarreal confirmed, and NAC had earned the tie by beating Groningen 3-1 on aggregate in the 2009 play-offs.

q: Which Turkish coach, the first from Turkey to hold a UEFA Pro Licence, was MVV's head coach from 2008 to 2010?
sub: He succeeded Robert Maaskant.
note: Capa, the Pro Licence first and succeeding Maaskant all confirmed. His exact leaving date in February 2010 is not supported by the sources, so the month is out.

q: MVV reached the 2017 play-off final by beating which Frisian club 3-2 on aggregate, with a stoppage-time goal from Thomas Verheydt?
sub: 1-1 in Maastricht, then 2-1 in Leeuwarden.
note: 1-1 in Maastricht, 2-1 in Leeuwarden with Verheydt scoring in the 93rd minute, confirmed. No source says it was a header, so that word is out.

q: FC Dordrecht went up in 2014 by winning the play-off final second leg 3-1 at the Krommedijk after a 2-2 first leg. Who did they beat?
sub: Dordrecht's first Eredivisie season since 1994-95, and they went straight back down.
note: 2-2 at Sparta then 3-1 at the Krommedijk confirmed. The nineteen years did not add up: the previous promotion was in 1994.

q: Who was Heracles' head coach from September 2014 to 2018, taking them into Europe for the first time?
sub: He later coached Go Ahead Eagles and PEC Zwolle.
note: Head coach from 1 September 2014 to 30 June 2018, Heracles first European tie came in 2016 on his watch, and he later coached Go Ahead Eagles and PEC Zwolle.

q: Which coach left Groningen in 2010 after eight years and went straight to Heerenveen, to the fury of Groningen fans?
sub: He later won the 2014 cup with PEC Zwolle.
note: Groningen from October 2002 to June 2010, terms agreed with Heerenveen in February 2010, and the 2014 cup with PEC Zwolle. Confirmed.

q: AZ's stadium opened in 2006 under which name, dropped in November 2009 when the sponsor bank collapsed?
sub: It became the AFAS Stadion in 2010.
note: Opened in 2006 as the DSB Stadion, the name came off on 4 November 2009 after the bank failed, AFAS from 2010. Confirmed.

q: Roda JC's Parkstad Limburg Stadion opened on 15 August 2000 with a 2-2 friendly against which Spanish club?
sub: It replaced the old Kaalheide ground.
note: Opened on 15 August 2000 with a 2-2 against Real Zaragoza, replacing Kaalheide. Confirmed.

q: Which club was the first in Dutch professional football to lay an artificial pitch in its stadium, in 2003?
sub: The plastic pitch lasted until 2024, when hybrid grass went in.
note: First Dutch professional club with an artificial pitch, in 2003, confirmed. The sub called the ground the Polman Stadion until 2024, but it was renamed Erve Asito in 2019.

q: Twente were relegated on 29 April 2018 after 34 years in the top flight. Which club beat them 5-0 that day?
sub: Eight years after the title.
note: Relegated on 29 April 2018 after losing 5-0 at Vitesse, 34 years up, eight years after the title. Confirmed by NOS.

q: Groningen won the club's first major trophy in the 2015 KNVB Cup final. Who was their coach?
sub: Groningen were the third club from the city to win a major honour.
note: The old question repeated row 27, which already states Groningen beat PEC Zwolle 2-0 in that final. Reworked onto a different fact from the same match, both confirmed on the 2015 final article.

q: Which coach won one of his eleven games as Cambuur went down in 2016, and was still handed the Ajax job in 2017?
sub: Ajax sacked him in December 2017 after a cup exit at Twente.
note: One win from eleven at Cambuur, then Ajax from 17 June 2017 and the sacking on 21 December after the cup exit at Twente. Confirmed.

q: Which Japanese forward, scorer of the winner against Spain at the 2012 Olympics, joined VVV-Venlo that August?
sub: He came from Borussia Moenchengladbach.
note: Winner against Spain and the move from Borussia Moenchengladbach on 31 August 2012 confirmed. Cut the Honda successor line: Honda had left Venlo nearly three years earlier.

q: Which coach quit Willem II in April 2011, four games from the end with the club bottom, after being told he would not be kept on?
sub: John Feskens and Raymond Vissers finished the season. Willem II ended on 15 points.
note: Heerkes leaving in April 2011 and the 15 points confirmed. Feskens did not do it alone, Raymond Vissers took over with him.

q: RKC's run of nineteen straight Eredivisie seasons ended in 2007 with a play-off defeat to which Limburg club?
sub: VVV won the decider 3-0 and went straight back down a year later.
note: Nineteen straight seasons and the VVV play-off confirmed, but the scores were wrong: it was settled in a deciding match that VVV won 3-0.

q: Which Brazilian scored seventy goals in seven seasons for Heracles and left Almelo for Al-Nassr in 2013?
sub: He became Heracles' all-time Eredivisie top scorer back in March 2010.
note: 70 goals in seven seasons and the Al-Nassr move in 2013 confirmed. Rephrased because record Eredivisie scorer was a live present-tense record.

q: Which club did Vitesse beat 6-2 away on 7 December 2013 during Peter Bosz's first season?
sub: Vitesse were top of the table that November.
note: PSV 2-6 Vitesse on 7 December 2013 in Bosz first season, and Vitesse did top the table in November 2013. Confirmed.

q: Which English club agreed in 2016 to loan NAC Breda four to six players a season for five years?
sub: Angelino spent the 2017-18 season in Breda under that deal.
note: The Manchester City deal, four to six players a season for five years, is confirmed on nl.wikipedia NAC. Angelino was loaned in July 2017, so first arrivals was wrong and Manu Garcia could not be confirmed.

q: Which coach relegated Roda JC in 2014 after being appointed in January, winning three of seventeen games?
sub: Roda's first relegation after 41 years in the top flight.
note: Appointed on 3 January 2014, three wins in seventeen, relegation after 41 seasons in the Eredivisie. Confirmed.

q: Which club did Willem II beat in the 2012 play-off final to go up, having already knocked out Sparta?
sub: Jurgen Streppel's first season in Tilburg.
note: Willem II beat Sparta and then FC Den Bosch in the 2012 play-offs, and it was Streppel first season. Confirmed.

q: Which German coach was sacked by NEC on 24 April 2017, two games from the end, after refusing to have a senior coach put alongside him?
sub: He called the board's plan panic football. NEC went down to NAC.
note: Sacked on 24 April 2017 with two games left, refused an experienced coach alongside him and called it panic football, and NEC went down to NAC. Confirmed.

q: Which Japanese defender left VVV-Venlo for Southampton in August 2012 for about three million pounds?
sub: He had followed Honda from Nagoya Grampus to Venlo in 2009.
note: Southampton on 30 August 2012 for about three million pounds, having come from Nagoya Grampus in December 2009. Confirmed.

q: Who coached Go Ahead Eagles to the 2016 promotion after arriving in February that year, and was sacked in March 2017 with the club bottom?
sub: Robert Maaskant saw out the relegation season.
note: Appointed 22 February 2016, promoted in May 2016, sacked 22 March 2017 with the club bottom, and Maaskant could not keep them up. Confirmed.

q: Go Ahead Eagles are called Kowet. Where does the name come from?
a: Deventer workers mangling the English name Go Ahead in their dialect
sub: The posh rival club UD laughed at the pronunciation, so the fans kept it as a badge of honour.
note: The UD class story and Kowet as a badge of honour are exactly what the source says.

q: Which shirt number do Go Ahead Eagles refuse to give to a player, and why?
a: Number 12, it belongs to the supporters as the twelfth man
note: The club site returns 403. Verified instead on nl.wikipedia Go Ahead Eagles: number 12 is not issued because the fans are the twelfth man. Only the source link changed.

q: Go Ahead's biggest ever win, 11-1 in October 1962, came against which Limburg club?
sub: Roda had only been formed that summer from Rapid JC and Roda Sport.
note: 11-1 on 7 October 1962 in Deventer, and Roda JC had been formed on 27 June 1962 from Roda Sport and Rapid JC. Confirmed.

q: A former Ajax, Arsenal and Barcelona winger came out of retirement at 35 to play the 2008-09 season for Go Ahead Eagles. Who?
sub: 24 games, no goals, and his knee gave up again after one season.
note: 24 games, no goals, one season, and his knee ended it. Confirmed.

q: De Graafschap won the 2010 Eerste Divisie title at home to Go Ahead after being 2-0 down. How did it end?
a: 3-2, with goals in the 86th and 89th minutes
sub: Muslu Nalbantoglu scored the winner in the 89th minute.
note: Confirmed on the match page: 4 April 2010 in Doetinchem, 2-0 down after 14 minutes, goals in the 86th and 89th. No source calls Nalbantoglu the captain or says he headed it.

q: Johan Voskamp made his Sparta debut on 20 August 2010 against Almere City. What did he do?
a: Scored eight goals in a 12-1 win
sub: He had joined from Helmond Sport that summer. The 12-1 equalled a Dutch record.
note: Eight goals on debut in the 12-1 confirmed. He signed ahead of the season, not earlier that week.

q: In the 2010 Rotterdam play-off at Sparta, Excelsior's Guyon Fernandez missed a late penalty and Sparta scored in stoppage time. Then what?
a: Fernandez equalised in the 94th minute, Excelsior went up on away goals and Sparta went down
note: Fernandez missed in the 88th, Poepon put Sparta ahead in the 92nd, Fernandez equalised in the 94th and Excelsior went up on away goals. All confirmed.

q: In 1974 Excelsior played with a large letter A on the shirt when shirt sponsors were banned. What was the A for?
a: Akai, the electronics firm paying them, though the club claimed it meant A-team
sub: Shirt sponsors were legal from 1982, and Akai went straight back on.
note: Akai, Rob Albers and the A-team excuse confirmed on nl.wikipedia SBV Excelsior. No source supports the two games count, so it is out.

q: Excelsior named a stand at Woudestein after a striker who spent two years in their youth academy before Feyenoord. Who?
note: The stand is named after Van Persie, who was in the Excelsior academy from 1997 to 1999. Confirmed.

q: In November 1970 Feyenoord keeper Eddy Treijtel killed a seagull with a goal kick at Het Kasteel. Why does that still annoy Sparta fans?
a: The stuffed bird is in Feyenoord's museum, not Sparta's
note: Treijtel shot down a seagull with a goal kick in November 1970 and the stuffed bird sits in the Feyenoord museum. Confirmed.

q: Which Rotterdam club had Georginio Wijnaldum, Memphis Depay and Kevin Strootman in its youth ranks before they became famous elsewhere?
sub: Strootman is the one who actually made the Sparta first team.
note: All three are confirmed Sparta academy products and Strootman played for the first team. The ages, thirteen and twelve, are not in any source I could open.

q: Heerenveen won 5-0 at Excelsior on 10 December 2011. What was remarkable about the scoring?
sub: He finished the season as top scorer with 32 and left for Wolfsburg.
note: All five goals at Excelsior on 10 December 2011, 32 goals as top scorer, Wolfsburg in June 2012. Confirmed.

q: Trond Sollied won Heerenveen their first ever major trophy, the 2009 KNVB Cup, in May. What happened to him on 31 August?
a: He was sacked, three months after winning the cup
note: Cup win and the sacking on 31 August 2009 confirmed. The four points from five games line is not in any source I could open, so it is gone.

q: Bonaventure Kalou scored in Heerenveen's 2009 cup final win. What did he get himself elected as in Ivory Coast in 2018?
sub: His younger brother Salomon also played for Feyenoord.
note: Goal in the 2009 final and mayor of Vavoua in 2018 confirmed. Swapped the sub for the brother fact the same source states, rather than the unverified Chelsea line.

q: The Abe Lenstra Stadion opened in August 1994 with Heerenveen against PSV. Which teenager made his European debut for PSV that day?
note: Opened on 20 August 1994 with a friendly against PSV, and it was Ronaldo first match in Europe. Confirmed.

q: What is played over the loudspeakers before every Heerenveen home league match?
sub: A tradition going back to a wartime match in 1943.
note: Could not verify. The cited page returns 403, and nl.wikipedia on SC Heerenveen, the Abe Lenstra Stadion and the Frisian anthem say nothing about the anthem being played before every home match or about a 1943 wartime origin.

q: AZ became champions on 19 April 2009 without playing. What had happened?
a: PSV beat Ajax 6-2, so nobody could catch AZ anymore
sub: AZ had lost 2-1 at Vitesse the day before.
note: PSV 6-2 Ajax on 19 April 2009 is listed among the season highest scoring games, AZ had lost 2-1 to Vitesse the day before and became champions without playing. Confirmed.

q: Why did the letters DSB come down off AZ's stadium in November 2009?
a: DSB Bank, the sponsor owned by chairman Dirk Scheringa, had gone bankrupt
sub: For that autumn's Champions League games it was called the Dirk Scheringa Stadion.
note: DSB came down on 4 November 2009 after the bank owned by chairman Dirk Scheringa failed, and UEFA rules meant Dirk Scheringa Stadion for the European games. Confirmed.

q: AZ beat PSV 2-1 on Saturday 28 September 2013. What did the club do to coach Gertjan Verbeek on the Sunday morning?
a: Sacked him, citing a lack of chemistry with the players
sub: Verbeek had won them the cup four months earlier.
note: Beat PSV 2-1 on Saturday 28 September 2013 and sacked Verbeek the next day citing no basis for cooperation with the squad. Confirmed by NOS.

q: Vitesse captain Guram Kashia wore a rainbow armband against Heracles in October 2017. What was the reaction back home in Georgia?
a: Protests outside the federation and calls to drop him from the national team
sub: UEFA gave him its first ever EqualGame award for it.
note: Rainbow armband against Heracles, protests at the Georgian federation with arrests, and the first UEFA EqualGame award. Confirmed.

q: Which Georgian businessman bought all the shares in Vitesse in August 2010?
sub: He bought out Maasbert Schouten and said he planned to spend all his money.
note: Jordania and the August 2010 takeover confirmed by NOS, but that report does not mention Abramovich and I could not verify the first foreign owner claim. A two-part answer also breaks the one-answer rule. Retiered to extreme because without the rumour it is a fact, not a gasp.

q: Vitesse waited 125 years for a first major trophy. Who scored both goals in the 2017 cup final, both in the last ten minutes?
sub: 2-0 against AZ, on 30 April 2017, under Henk Fraser.
note: Both goals, in the 81st and 88th minutes, 2-0 against AZ on 30 April 2017 under Henk Fraser, a first trophy in 125 years. Confirmed.

q: On 7 July 2011 part of the roof of De Grolsch Veste collapsed during building work. What was the human cost?
a: Two construction workers died and fourteen were injured
sub: The safety board found essential parts of the roof structure were missing.
note: Two construction workers were killed in the roof collapse. Nothing in the deck should trade on a death.

q: In May 2016 the KNVB licensing committee took Twente's Eredivisie licence away and put them in the Eerste Divisie. How did Twente stay up?
a: They won on appeal in June and got a fine of 181,000 euros instead
note: Licence withdrawn in May 2016 and restored on appeal on 17 June 2016 with a 181,000 euro fine for four violations. Confirmed by the KNVB.

q: Twente trailed Ajax 2-1 early in the second half of the 2011 KNVB Cup final. How did it finish?
a: 3-2 to Twente after extra time, Marc Janko scoring in the 117th minute
sub: Nacer Chadli and Roy Beerens got the other Twente goals.
note: Two errors. Ajax were never 2-0 up after 40 minutes: Nakamura scored in the 24th and Vertonghen in the 52nd. And Twente's other scorers were Chadli and Beerens, not Brama and Janssen. Janko's winner came in the 117th minute and no source calls it a header.

q: Twente sold Ola John to Benfica in 2012. Which investment fund was reported to have taken about 80 percent of the fee?
a: Doyen Sports, an investment fund that part-owned the player
sub: The fund part-owned the player. The Doyen deals fed the crisis that nearly sank Twente.
note: Wikipedia calls the 80 percent share a rumour rather than something the leaked documents proved, so the claim is softened to reported.

q: The 2014 KNVB Cup final was stopped in the fifth minute with Ajax 1-0 up against PEC Zwolle. Why, and how did it end?
a: Ajax fans threw fireworks on the pitch, and after a half-hour break PEC won 5-1
note: Stopped in the fifth minute with Ajax 1-0 up through Van Rhijn, fireworks from the Ajax end, half hour break, 5-1 to PEC. Confirmed.

q: Where does the name Cambuur come from?
a: The Camminghaburg, a castle of the Van Cammingha family that stood where the stadium was built
sub: The combs on the badge are a pun on the family name Cammingha.
note: The Camminghaburg origin is confirmed. The badge is not simply the family coat of arms: nl.wikipedia describes a red deer with combs as speaking arms punning on Cammingha.

q: FC Dordrecht fans are the Schapenkoppen, the sheep heads. What is the story behind it?
a: Two men tried to smuggle a dressed-up sheep past the city gates in 1866 and it bleated
note: The 1866 sheep in scarecrow clothes that gave itself away by bleating at the city gate. Confirmed.

q: De Graafschap put seats on the Spinnekop terrace in the late 1990s. What did the club do in 2008?
a: Took the seats out again after supporter protests
sub: The name comes from the Spion Kop, the Boer War hill.
note: Seats went on the Spinnekop in the 1998 rebuild and came out again in 2008 after protests, and the name comes from the Spion Kop. Confirmed.

q: NAC's stadium is named after Antoon Verlegh. How did he get the nickname Rat?
a: He played like a ratje, sly and hard to knock off the ball
sub: His mother hated the nickname.
note: The nickname and his mother hating it are confirmed. The source says sly, skilful and hard to dispossess, not small and quick.

q: Cyriel Dessers played four play-off matches for NAC in 2017. How many goals did he score in them?
a: Seven, including a hat-trick in the 4-1 win at NEC
note: Seven goals in four play-off matches including the hat-trick at NEC, confirmed by the source. Retiered: a strong stat, but the table will not gasp at a number, so it belongs in extreme.

q: NEC's German coach Peter Hyballa was sacked in April 2017 two games before the end. What had he turned down?
a: The board wanted to put an experienced coach next to him, he called it panic football
note: Duplicate. Row 67 already asks about the same sacking and carries the same panic football line, and each row gives away the other.

q: Alireza Jahanbakhsh scored two late goals at Ajax on the last day of 2013-14 to keep NEC out of the automatic relegation places. And then?
a: NEC lost the play-off and went down anyway
note: Two late goals at Ajax on the final day and the play-off relegation confirmed. Took Sparta out of the answer so it no longer gives away the answer to another row.

q: Roda JC took on a Dubai-based investor in January 2017 who brought Nicolas Anelka in as adviser. What happened to the investor within weeks?
a: Aleksei Korotaev was arrested in Dubai over an uncovered cheque of 17.7 million euros
note: Korotaev, the Anelka advisory role and the Dubai detention from February 2017 confirmed. The cheque was 17.7 million euros, so about 17 million rounded the wrong way.

q: Daryl Werker scored for MVV in the 2016 play-offs while on loan from Roda. What did he do in the 2017 play-off final?
a: Headed the only goal of the tie for Roda JC against MVV
sub: 0-0 in Maastricht, 1-0 in Kerkrade, Roda stayed up.
note: One goal in four play-off games for MVV on loan in 2016, then the only goal of the 2017 tie for Roda, 0-0 in Maastricht and 1-0 in Kerkrade. Confirmed.

q: MVV lost 3-1 at home to Almere City in the 2018 play-offs. What was odd about Almere's hat-trick hero Damon Mirani?
a: A central defender, he scored with his left foot, his right foot and his head
note: MVV 1-3 Almere City on 1 May 2018 and the perfect hat-trick by a centre back confirmed. The source says he had four career goals before it, not that it was his first hat-trick, so that claim is out.

q: In 2010 MVV changed what the M stands for. It had been Maastrichtse. What did it become?
a: Maatschappelijke, the socially responsible football club
sub: The full name became Maatschappelijke Voetbal Vereniging Maastricht.
note: The 2010 change from Maastrichtse to Maatschappelijke is confirmed. The bankruptcy rescue framing in the old sub is not in the source, so it has been replaced.

q: MVV's hardcore stand is the Angel Side. Which angel?
a: The angel in the coat of arms of the city of Maastricht
sub: The city arms show an armed angel holding a red shield with a white star.
note: The Angel Side and the city arms are confirmed, but the source dates the group to the 1980s and says nothing about 1976 or the south-west corner.

q: VVV-Venlo play at De Koel. What does koel mean in Venlo dialect, and why is it apt?
a: A pit or hollow, the ground is literally built in one, with the stands on its sides
sub: Players walk down a long staircase from the dressing rooms to the pitch.
note: Koel is Venlo dialect for pit, the ground sits in a former excavation and the long staircase down from the dressing rooms is famous. Confirmed.

q: On 11 September 2011 a VVV-Venlo defender scored a spectacular bicycle kick against PSV in a 3-3 draw. Who was he?
sub: He went to Southampton a year later.
note: Bicycle kick from a corner against PSV on 11 September 2011 in a 3-3 draw, Goal of the Season, Southampton a year later. Confirmed.

q: What did VVV-Venlo fans nickname Keisuke Honda in his 2008-09 promotion season?
note: Keizer Keisuke, Emperor Keisuke, is on the English Honda article. Confirmed.

q: Fortuna Sittard suspended coach Sunday Oliseh in February 2018 while second in the table. What was his explanation?
a: He said he was removed for refusing to take part in illegal activities at the club
sub: The club only said he had been put on non-active. Fortuna went up anyway.
note: His illegal activities explanation is confirmed, but the club statement said only that he was put on non-active, it did not cite working with management.

q: In 2016 the KNVB confirmed match-fixing in a 2009 Eredivisie game, a Willem II defeat at Utrecht. Which player made the deal?
a: Ibrahim Kargbo, with fixer Wilson Raj Perumal
sub: Utrecht won that match 1-0 on 9 August 2009.
note: Kargbo and Perumal confirmed by NOS, along with the match. The De Volkskrant line about the Ajax and Feyenoord games is not in the source, so it is replaced.

q: In 2016 ADO Den Haag took its own majority owner to court over unpaid promised money. Who was he?
a: Wang Hui of United Vansen, the Chinese company that took over the club in 2015
sub: The Enterprise Chamber suspended him as supervisory board chairman in December 2016.
note: Wang Hui, the court case over about two million euros and the suspension on 19 December 2016 confirmed. The shares passed to United Vansen on 27 January 2015, not in 2014.

q: ADO beat Groningen 5-1 at home in the 2011 play-off final for a Europa League place. What happened in the return?
a: Groningen won 5-1 too, and ADO won the shoot-out with ten men
sub: ADO had Mitchell Pique sent off in the 88th minute of the second leg.
note: 5-1 at the Kyocera, 5-1 to Groningen in the return, ADO through 4-3 on penalties with ten men, all confirmed. The Matavz hitting the bar detail is not in the source.

q: Utrecht lost the first leg of the 2017 European play-off final 3-0 at AZ. How did the second leg go?
a: Utrecht won 3-0, AZ keeper Tim Krul saved a stoppage-time penalty, and Utrecht won the shoot-out 4-3
note: 3-0 down then 3-0 up, Krul saving Haller penalty in the last minute and Utrecht winning 4-3 on penalties confirmed. The old answer read as if Krul were the Utrecht keeper.

q: What is wrong with the city coat of arms on FC Utrecht's badge?
a: The diagonal runs the wrong way, it is mirrored
sub: It happened in September 1982 and has never been properly explained.
note: The mirrored city arms are confirmed. The printing error and cost story is only one of several accounts, none of them settled, so the sub no longer states it as fact.

q: Frans van Seumeren bought 63 percent of FC Utrecht in April 2008. Which Feyenoord legend did he sack as coach that December?
note: Van Seumeren took 63 percent of the shares for 16 million euros in April 2008 and Van Hanegem was sacked on 23 December 2008. Confirmed.

q: What does Galgenwaard, the name of FC Utrecht's ground, mean?
sub: The rebuilt 1982 stadium was famous for the dry moats around the pitch.
note: Galghenwert was a gallows field where the bodies of the executed hung until about 1600. The 1982 ground is described as having dry moats, plural.

q: After a 0-0 at Aberdeen in 2014, Groningen's Filip Kostic said they had done 80 percent of the job. What happened in the return?
a: Groningen lost 2-1 at home and went out
sub: Aberdeen's Jonny Hayes said he enjoyed ramming the words down their throats.
note: Legs were the wrong way round. The 0-0 was at Pittodrie on 17 July 2014 and Aberdeen won 2-1 at the Euroborg on 24 July. Kostic and the Hayes quote are confirmed.

q: Besides football, what can you find inside Groningen's Euroborg complex?
a: A casino, a cinema, a school, a supermarket and a gym
note: Casino, cinema, school, supermarket and fitness centre inside the Euroborg complex. Confirmed.

q: Volendam finished bottom of the Eredivisie in 2008-09, yet reached the cup semi-finals. Which giant did they beat 1-0 in round three?
sub: Jack Tuijp scored in the 111th minute at the Kras Stadion.
note: Bottom place, the cup semi-final run and the 1-0 over Ajax in round three confirmed, with Tuijp scoring in the 111th minute. The best moments of his career quote is not in any source I could open.

q: Which striker scored 176 goals for Volendam and, in a later spell at Helmond Sport, finished a match in goal?
sub: Helmond had used all their subs and their keeper had been sent off.
note: 176 goals for Volendam, second behind great-uncle Dick Tol on 276, confirmed. The old wording implied he was a Volendam player at Helmond, but he was playing for Helmond Sport against Telstar in 2014-15. Also rephrased away from a present-tense all-time claim.

q: NEC sacked Alex Pastoor on 19 August 2013, the earliest sacking in an Eredivisie season. What had just happened?
a: A 5-1 home defeat to PEC Zwolle
note: Sacked on 19 August 2013, two days after a 5-1 home defeat by PEC Zwolle, described as the fastest sacking in an Eredivisie season. Confirmed.

q: Marinus Dijkhuizen took Excelsior up in 2014 and kept them up. How long did his next job, at Brentford in 2015, last?
a: Nine matches, and he was gone by the end of September
sub: Two wins, two draws and five defeats.
note: Promotion in 2014 and survival in 2014-15 confirmed, and Brentford let him go on 28 September 2015 after nine games. The 47 days does not work from any dates I can find, since he was announced on 1 June.

q: Dwight Lodeweges coached Cambuur in the Eredivisie in 2013-14. Where did he go on 1 April 2014, with the season still running?
a: To Heerenveen, the Frisian derby rivals
note: The move to Heerenveen on 1 April 2014 is confirmed, but Lodeweges did not take Cambuur up in 2013: Alfons Arts, then Henk de Jong and Jan Bruin, won that title. He arrived for the Eredivisie season.

q: Willem II's Spanish striker Fran Sol, a Real Madrid youth product, published something unusual in 2020. What?
sub: He also learned French, Dutch, English and Russian.
note: Madrid 2035 in 2020, a Real Madrid youth product at Willem II, and four learned languages. Confirmed.

q: Why is Twente's ground called a Veste, a fortress?
a: Grolsch comes from Groenlo, an old fortified town
sub: Until 2008 it was the Arke Stadion, after a travel company.
note: Veste means fortress and points at Groenlo, the fortified town where Grolsch was first brewed, and it was the Arke Stadion until 2008. Confirmed. Retiered: good etymology, but nobody at the table gasps, so extreme not ball.

q: Heracles trailed Groningen 3-1 on aggregate with eight minutes left in the 2016 European play-off semi-final. Final aggregate?
a: 6-3 to Heracles, after a 5-1 second leg in extra time
sub: Zomer, Gladon, Weghorst, Darri and Pelupessy scored.
note: 2-1 to Groningen at the Euroborg, then 5-1 to Heracles after extra time for 6-3, with all five scorers as listed. Confirmed.
